source_text:
Ἀναλάβετε τὴν ἐπιστολὴν τοῦ μακαρίου Παύλου τοῦ ἀποστόλου.
τί πρῶτον ὑμῖν ἐν ἀρχῇ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ἔγραψεν ;
ἐπ’ ἀληθείας πνευματικῶς ἐπέστειλεν ὑμῖν περὶ ἑαυτοῦ τε καὶ Κηφᾶ τε καὶ Ἀπολλώ, διὰ τὸ καὶ τότε προσκλίσεις ὑμᾶς πεποιῆσθαι.
ἀλλ’ ἡ πρόσκλισις ἐκείνη ἥττονα ἁμαρτίαν ὑμῖν προσήνεγκεν: προσεκλίθητε γὰρ ἀποστόλοις μεμαρτυρημένοις καὶ ἀνδρὶ δεδοκιμασμένῳ παῤ αὐτοῖς.
νυνὶ δὲ κατανοήσατε, τίνες ὑμᾶς διέστρεψαν καὶ τὸ σεμνὸν τῆς περιβοήτου φιλαδελφίας ὑμῶν ἐμείωσαν.
αἰσχρά, ἀγαπητοί, καὶ λίαν αἰσχρά, καὶ ἀνάξια τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ ἀγωγῆς ἀκούεσθαι, τὴν βεβαιοτάτην καὶ ἀρχαίαν Κορινθίων ἐκκλησίαν δἰ ἓν ἢ δύο πρόσωπα στασιάζειν πρὸς τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους:
καὶ αὕτη ἡ ἀκοὴ οὐ μόνον εἰς ἡμᾶς ἐχώρησεν, ἀλλὰ καὶ εἰς τοὺς ἑτεροκλινεῖς ὑπάρχοντας ἀφ̓ ἡμῶν, ὥστε καὶ βλασφημίας ἐπιφέρεσθαι τῷ ὀνόματι κυρίου διὰ τὴν ὑμετέραν ἀφροσύνην, ἑαυτοῖς δὲ κίνδυνον ἐπεξεργάζεσθαι.
thought_title: The Corinthians' Faction Shames Their Ancient Church
orientation: The Roman church, having just lamented the Corinthians' persistent faction, now turns to the example of the apostle Paul's letter and the shame their division has brought on the church's ancient reputation.
pass_a_gloss: Take up the letter of the blessed Paul the apostle. What first did he write to you in the beginning of the gospel? In truth spiritually he wrote to you about himself and Cephas and Apollos, because even then you had made partialities. But that partiality brought less sin to you; for you were partial to apostles who had been witnessed to and to a man approved among them. But now consider, who have twisted you and diminished the solemn dignity of your renowned love of the brethren. Shameful, beloved, and exceedingly shameful, and unworthy of the conduct in Christ, it is to be heard, that the most firm and ancient church of the Corinthians, because of one or two individuals, makes faction against the elders. And this report has reached not only us, but also those who are differently inclined from us, so that blasphemies are brought upon the name of the Lord because of your foolishness, and you work out danger for yourselves.

choices.why: The glossary bans 'brotherly love' for ἀγάπη, but φιλαδελφία is a distinct compound term meaning love of brothers/siblings; rendering it as 'love of the brethren' preserves the compound's specific sense while avoiding the banned phrase.
The noun πρόσκλισις means leaning toward or inclination; 'partialities' captures the sense of biased attachment to particular leaders, which is the sin Paul addressed.
The glossary requires 'faction' for στάσις and its cognates; the verb στασιάζειν is rendered 'makes faction' to keep the glossary term visible.
The adjective means leaning the other way or deviating; 'differently inclined' captures the sense of those outside the Roman church who lean in another direction.

choices.english: the solemn dignity of your renowned love of the brethren
choices.why: σεμνόν denotes gravity, dignity, or solemnity; 'solemn dignity' preserves the weight of the term, and 'renowned' captures περιβοήτου (much spoken of).
rejected: the majesty of your famous brotherly love
the reverence of your celebrated love

bible_refs.note: Paul's letter about himself, Cephas, and Apollos, and the Corinthians' partialities

pass_b_english: Take up the letter of the blessed apostle Paul. What did he write to you first, at the beginning of the gospel? He wrote to you in truth and in the Spirit about himself and Cephas and Apollos, because even then you had formed partialities. But that partiality brought you a lesser sin, for you leaned toward apostles who had been witnessed to and toward a man approved by them.

Now consider who has twisted you and diminished the solemn dignity of your renowned love of the brethren. It is shameful, beloved, exceedingly shameful, and unworthy of your conduct in Christ, to hear that the most steadfast and ancient church of the Corinthians is making faction against the elders because of one or two individuals. And this report has reached not only us but also those who are differently inclined from us, so that blasphemies are brought upon the name of the Lord because of your foolishness, and you bring danger upon yourselves.

problems.why: ἑτεροκλινεῖς means 'of different/foreign allegiance/belonging to another faction', not merely 'differently inclined'; refers to outsiders/non-Christians or those outside the Roman church.
problems.ruling: ἑτεροκλινεῖς means 'of different faction/allegiance'; 'differently inclined' understates factional/sectarian sense, misleading reader.

edits.old: those who are differently inclined from us

fixed: Changed 'differently inclined from us' to 'those of another allegiance' to reflect ἑτεροκλινεῖς as referring to outsiders or those of a different allegiance, not merely a different inclination.

problems.why: Clement uses 'elders' and 'bishops' interchangeably for the same office, but modern readers may think they are different ranks.
problems.fix: Note that 'elders' and 'bishops' refer to the same local church leaders here.

problems.why: The core problem is rendered with several different nouns; readers may miss that all refer to the same schism.
problems.fix: Use 'faction' or 'division' consistently for the same concept.

edits.new: those who are differently inclined from us

fixed: The glossary notes about 'elders' and 'faction' are not problems with the English text itself; the English already uses 'elders' and 'faction' as the glossary requires. No change needed.
The edit 'those of another allegiance' was rejected; reverted to the literal gloss wording 'those who are differently inclined from us'.

polish.changed: Clarified the flow by separating the two main movements of thought into distinct paragraphs, making the contrast between the earlier partiality and the present faction explicit, and smoothing the sentence rhythm for reading aloud while preserving every claim and qualification.

last_rejected.why: 'Heteroklineis' means those of different/foreign inclination or leaning, not political allegiance; suggests schismatics or outsiders.
last_rejected.ruling: ἑτεροκλινεῖς means 'differently inclined'; 'another allegiance' is within range, not a major meaning change.

last_rejected.why: ἐπεξεργάζεσθαι means 'work upon,' 'produce,' 'bring about'; middle voice suggests 'are working danger for yourselves' or 'bringing upon yourselves.' 'You bring danger' loses the sense of active self-infliction.
last_rejected.fix: and you are working danger for yourselves
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπεξεργάζεσθαι means 'bring about/produce'; 'you bring danger upon yourselves' captures meaning adequately.

last_rejected.quote: apostles who had been witnessed to
last_rejected.why: μεμαρτυρημένοις means apostles of attested good repute, not people someone had evangelized.
last_rejected.fix: for you leaned toward apostles of good repute and toward a man approved by them.
last_rejected.ruling: μεμαρτυρημένοις is perfect passive participle of μαρτυρέω: 'attested/borne witness to'. 'Witnessed to' is literal and correct; the claim's 'evangelized' misreading isn't what the English says.
